step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify Nodes: The visual diagram and transcript focus on Foodhub's order processing and analytics workflow. The RESTAURANT node represents the EPOS system actor (UserCompanyAgent). Connected to it are AMPLIFY (Amplify), APPSYNC (AppSync), LAMBDA (Lambda), DYNAMODB (DynamoDB), KINESIS (Kinesis), S3 (S3), and QUICKSIGHT (QuickSight). The CUSTOMER actor is on the whiteboard but unconnected and inactive in this primary workflow, so it is pruned per Node Rule 5.
2. Identify Edges and Workflows:
   - Flow 0 (Order Processing & Syncing): RESTAURANT sends data to AMPLIFY SDK on EPOS machines -> AMPLIFY syncs with APPSYNC -> APPSYNC triggers LAMBDA resolvers -> LAMBDA writes order state to DYNAMODB.
   - Flow 1 (Real-time Analytics & Dashboarding): DYNAMODB streams updates to KINESIS via DynamoDB Streams -> KINESIS outputs data into S3 data lake -> QUICKSIGHT reads from S3 to present real-time dashboards for restaurant owners and back-office operations.

graph.name: Foodhub Real-time Order Processing and Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: Foodhub processes millions of restaurant orders using a serverless backend with AppSync and Lambda, streaming DynamoDB updates via Kinesis to S3 and QuickSight for real-time operational insights.

nodes.name: RESTAURANT
nodes.notes: EPOS machine situated at restaurant locations used to process and sync orders across kitchen workstations.

nodes.name: AMPLIFY
nodes.notes: Amplify SDK built into EPOS devices for handling order synchronization.

nodes.name: APPSYNC
nodes.notes: AWS AppSync manages real-time data synchronization across all restaurant EPOS devices.

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: Lambda resolvers execute logic for order syncing, notifications, and dashboarding.

nodes.name: DYNAMODB
nodes.notes: Fully managed NoSQL database storing order state and accommodating rapid weekend traffic spikes.

nodes.name: KINESIS
nodes.notes: Receives change data captured via DynamoDB Streams for real-time analytics streaming.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central data lake storing order records for ETL processing and historical analysis.

nodes.name: QUICKSIGHT
nodes.notes: Business intelligence dashboarding tool for restaurant owners and back-office teams.

edges.notes: Restaurant EPOS machines use embedded Amplify SDK to send order data.
Amplify SDK communicates order sync requests to AWS AppSync.
AppSync triggers Lambda resolvers to handle business logic.
Lambda writes order state into DynamoDB.
DynamoDB Streams outputs order events into Kinesis.
Kinesis streams data directly into S3 data lake.
QuickSight queries S3 data lake to generate real-time analytics dashboards.
